get.summary: Get the project's usage in a month
get.description: Needs the `usage:read` scope (live keys only). The key's project in one UTC month: billable is accepted minus suppressed. `organization.state` says where the organization stands against its plan's monthly limit this month, without its numbers. `apiKey` is the calling key's own month in its current project, by the day its messages were accepted; informative, never another key's. A key moved from another project counts here from the move on.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: yyyy-MM, a UTC month; the current month when left out.

post.description: Needs the `emails:send` scope. Stores one message per recipient and answers 202 with their ids, in the order of `to`, `cc`, `bcc`. A recipient on the suppression list is accepted but not sent, and listed in `suppressed`. The sender's domain must be verified. A test key (`pk_test_`) never sends: its messages get simulated events. In the sandbox, live mail goes only to the organization's members and verified domains (422 `sandbox_recipient_not_allowed`), within a daily and a per-minute limit (429 with `Retry-After`). A project can have a daily and a per-minute limit of its own (429 `project_daily_limit_reached`, `project_rate_limit_reached`). The organization's plan limits the month, the day and the minute (429 `plan_monthly_limit_reached`, `plan_daily_limit_reached`, `plan_rate_limit_reached`). Only live recipients that aren't suppressed count. Apart from any plan, the platform limits each key and each project per minute and each project per day (429 `platform_rate_limit_reached`, `platform_daily_limit_reached`), far above every plan's limits. A message is at most 10 MB (413 `message_too_large`) and its size times its recipients at most 25 MB (413 `message_too_large_for_recipients`); a request body over 21 MB is not read (413 `payload_too_large`). While the platform's storage is low it takes no new messages (503 `service_degraded`, with `Retry-After`). `cc` and `bcc` take only exactly one `to` (422 `cc_bcc_require_single_to`); bcc recipients appear in no header. `headers` adds up to 10 of your own (`List-Unsubscribe`, `List-Unsubscribe-Post`, `In-Reply-To`, `References`, `X-`); any other, or one that breaks a rule, answers 400 under `errors.headers`. `sendAt` schedules the message: an ISO 8601 time with `Z` or an offset, at least a minute and at most 30 days ahead (422 `send_at_too_soon`, `send_at_too_far`; without an offset 400 under `errors.sendAt`). It waits with status `scheduled` and goes out at that time; the limits count then, not now. A project holds at most 10,000 scheduled messages of 256 MB together (409 `scheduled_limit_reached`, `scheduled_size_limit_reached`). Cancel one with `DELETE /v1/emails/{id}`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: 1 to 256 characters. A repeat within 24 hours answers as the first request did, without sending again.

post.description: Needs the `emails:send` scope. Sends one test email from a verified domain to one address of your own: an address a member confirmed for test emails in the project's portal (Test mail), or a member's address; any other is refused (422 `test_recipient_not_confirmed`). Without `subject`, `text` and `html` it sends Postilio's sample message. A project sends a few test emails per UTC day (429 `test_mail_daily_limit_reached`, with `Retry-After`). Otherwise it is a send like `POST /v1/emails`: the same limits, sandbox and sizes apply and it counts towards your usage. The message is listed with `via` `test_mail`; follow it with `GET /v1/emails/{id}`.

get.summary: Get an email and its events
get.description: Needs the `emails:read` scope. A test key finds only test messages and a live key only live ones; the other mode's are 404. A scheduled message shows its `sendAt`.

delete.description: Needs the `emails:send` scope. Cancels a message sent with `sendAt` while it waits: it gets status `canceled` and a `canceled` event, and its content is deleted. Once it is on its way, or for a message that was never scheduled, the answer is 409 `email_not_scheduled`. A test key finds only test messages and a live key only live ones; the other mode's are 404.

post.description: Needs the `domains:manage` scope. Answers the domain as `pending`, with the two CNAME records to create in its DNS. postilio.eu and names under it cannot be added. 409 `domain_exists` when the project has it already, 409 `domain_limit_reached` when the organization's plan allows no more domains.

delete.description: Needs the `domains:manage` scope. Mail from the domain stops at once.

post.summary: Check a domain's DNS records now
post.description: Needs the `domains:manage` scope. Checks now instead of at the next periodic check (every 10 minutes) and answers the domain's new state. Once a minute per domain: 429 `too_many_checks` with `Retry-After`. 503 `dns_unavailable` when DNS gave no answer.

get.description: Needs the `suppressions:manage` scope. Newest first; pass `next` as `before` for the next page.

post.description: Needs the `suppressions:manage` scope. Adds the address with reason `manual`. 409 `address_already_suppressed` when it is on the list already.

delete.description: Needs the `suppressions:manage` scope. A complaint is removed only with a reason, `{"reason": "…"}` of 10 to 500 characters; without one the answer is 422 `reason_required`. A hard bounce or manual entry needs no body.

post.description: Needs the `webhooks:manage` scope. The answer holds the signing secret, the only time it is shown. At most 10 endpoints per project, and as many for the organization as its plan allows: 409 `webhook_endpoint_limit_reached`.

patch.description: Needs the `webhooks:manage` scope. Only the fields you send change. `paused: false` resumes a paused endpoint.

post.description: Needs the `webhooks:manage` scope. Answers the new secret once. The old one keeps signing as well for 24 hours.
Needs the `webhooks:manage` scope. One `webhook.test.v1` delivery, tried once without retries, also to a paused endpoint.

get.description: Needs the `webhooks:manage` scope. Newest first; pass `next` as `before` for the next page.

post.description: Needs the `webhooks:manage` scope. One more attempt now, with the same id and payload. 409 `delivery_still_pending` while it is still being retried, `endpoint_paused` while the endpoint is paused.

accepted.description: Messages the key had accepted, one per recipient.

suppressed.description: Accepted but never sent, because the address is suppressed.

delivered.description: Delivered now; one with a complaint after delivery counts as complained instead.

ApiKeyMonthUsage.description:
The calling key in the month: its messages by the UTC day they were accepted and their status now, so a late bounce
counts in the month the message was accepted in. Informative; the project's numbers are what is billed.

billable.description: Accepted minus suppressed: what is billed.

final.description: The month is closed: these numbers no longer change.

resetsAt.description: The start of the next month, 00:00 UTC.

ApiUsage.description: The key's project in one UTC month, and where its organization stands; never the organization's own numbers.

plan.description: The code of the plan the organization has now.

state.description: As in the portal: `ok`, `warning`, `over` or `capped` for the current month, null for another one.

name.description: A host name of at least two labels, such as `mail.example.com`; not an IP address, not under postilio.eu.

secret.description: The signing secret (whsec_…). Shown once: it is stored encrypted and never returned again.

address.description: One bare address, at most 254 characters.

url.description: An absolute `https://` URL on a public address, at most 2048 characters, without credentials or a fragment.

events.description: One or more of: accepted, queued, delivered, deferred, bounced, expired, complained, suppressed, scheduled, canceled.

status.description:
missing (no record), invalid (receivers ignore it), monitoring (p=none: reports only) or enforced
    (p=quarantine or p=reject).

policyDomain.description:
Where the record was found: the domain itself or, for a subdomain without its own, a parent
    domain; null while missing.

records.description: The DMARC records found there, as published.

issues.description:
Why it is invalid: multiple_records, version (does not start with v=DMARC1), no_policy (no p= tag) or
    syntax. Advice on a valid one: no_reports (p=none without rua=, so nobody sees the reports) or spf_strict (aspf=s: SPF
    cannot align with the return path on bounce.<domain>, so DMARC rests on DKIM alone).

status.description: found, missing, or unknown until the first check.

DomainList.description: A list in an object, so paging can be added without breaking clients.

addedBy.description: The name of the dashboard user who added it; null when it was added with an API key.

failingSince.description: Since when its records are missing, while it is failing.

sent30d.description: Live messages sent from it today and the 29 days before (UTC); test and suppressed ones not.

contentType.description: A MIME type such as `application/pdf`, optionally with parameters.

contentId.description: Makes the attachment inline; the HTML refers to it as `cid:` plus this value.

via.description: `api`, `smtp`, or `test_mail` for a test email: how the message was submitted.

sendAt.description: When it is scheduled to go out (`sendAt` of the request); null when it was sent at once.

smtpCode.description: The receiving server's reply code; null when no server replied, such as when no connection could be made.

response.description: The receiving server's reply, with addresses and IP addresses masked; when no server replied, a sentence that explains what happened.

reason.description: Why the attempt was delayed or failed, as a stable code (see Delivery status in the docs), such as `tls_certificate_invalid`, `mailbox_full` or `recipient_server_temporary`; null when there is nothing to explain.

async.description: True for a report that arrived after delivery: a bounce the recipient's mail server sent later (reason `async_bounce`); null otherwise.

message.description: Only with some codes: a sentence for people, such as the limit that was crossed.

reason.description: Required, at least 10 characters, when the entry is a complaint; kept with the removal.

secret.description: The new signing secret, shown once.

previousSecretExpiresAt.description: Until then deliveries are signed with the old secret as well.

from.description: An address on a verified domain of the key's project, optionally with a display name (without '@' or ',').

to.description: 1 to 50 bare addresses, without display names; each gets a message of its own.

subject.description: At most 998 characters, without control characters.

tag.description: Optional; at most 64 letters, digits, '-' or '_'.

replyTo.description: Optional; one address, with or without a display name.

attachments.description: Optional; one with a `contentId` is inline, for `cid:` references in the HTML. The message, attachments included, is at most 10 MB, and its size times its recipients at most 25 MB (413).

cc.description: Optional; bare addresses, only with exactly one `to` (422 `cc_bcc_require_single_to`). Every copy shows them in its Cc header, and each gets a message of its own.

bcc.description: Optional; bare addresses, only with exactly one `to`. Never in any header; each gets a message of its own. `to`, `cc` and `bcc` together hold at most 50 addresses, each once.

headers.description: Optional; at most 10 extra headers: `List-Unsubscribe`, `List-Unsubscribe-Post`, `In-Reply-To`, `References` and `X-` headers. Values are printable ASCII, at most 900 characters; headers Postilio sets itself cannot be set (see Custom headers in the docs).

sendAt.description: Optional; when to send it, ISO 8601 with `Z` or an offset, such as `2026-11-02T09:00:00+01:00`: at least a minute and at most 30 days ahead (422 `send_at_too_soon`, `send_at_too_far`). Until then the message is `scheduled` and can be canceled with `DELETE /v1/emails/{id}`. Not over SMTP.

ids.description: One message per recipient, in the order of `to`, then `cc`, then `bcc`.

suppressed.description: Recipients on the project's suppression list: accepted with status `suppressed`, not sent.

next.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; null on the last page.

detail.description: The remote server's answer for a bounce, or who added it.

sourceMessageId.description: The message that caused it; it may already be gone from the log.

from.description: An address on a verified domain of the project.

to.description: One address: confirmed for test mail in the project, or a member's of its organization.

subject.description: With `text` or `html`, your own message; without all three, Postilio's sample message.

paused.description: true pauses the endpoint, false resumes it.

UpdateWebhookEndpointRequest.description: Every field is optional; what is left out stays as it is.

next.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; null on the last page.

eventId.description: The webhook-id header: the same for every attempt.

responseSnippet.description: The start of the last response body, at most 256 characters.

events.description: The message events it gets: accepted, queued, delivered, deferred, bounced, expired, complained, suppressed, scheduled, canceled.

mode.description: `live`, or `test`: a test endpoint gets the events of test-key messages only.

failingSince.description: Every attempt since then failed; after 72 hours of that the endpoint is paused.

secretHint.description: The last characters of the signing secret.

previousSecretExpiresAt.description: Until then the secret from before the last rotation still signs as well.

statusCode.description: The receiver's HTTP status; null when no answer came (timeout, refused, blocked address).

status.description: The delivery's status now: `pending` (to be retried), `delivered` or `failed`.

Bearer.description: An API key: pk_live_… or pk_test_…
